text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong in Phnom Penh to forge business ties.
- Singapore looks forward to welcoming Cambodia into ASEAN family next year and is pleased to see country rebuilding itself, Goh says.
- Government has accepted Cost Review Committee's report.
- Two property agents duped owner of luxury condominium unit into selling apartment for Singapore $1.27 million, knowing there was higher offer.
- Singapore Airlines to sell Raffles City stakes to DBS Land for at least S$100 million.
- Government of Singapore Investment Corpo regional manager suspended from duties on October 14 in view of investigations by the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau.
- Ringgit hits seven-month low against U.S. dollar on Malaysian corporate demand and stoploss selling by many offshore players.
- Precision optical and laser instruments maker Avimo Group shuts down Penang plant and will move all operations there back to Singapore.
- Managing director and chief investment officer of Schroders Singapore, Maggie Lee, promoted to main board of UK-headquartered Schroder Investment Management, first Asian to hold position.
- Footwear and sporting goods maker and distributor Ossia International offers 50 million shares at S$0.61 each.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton stays ahead as American go to polls.
- Bid by Ho Wah Genting's major shareholders to sell majority stake scuttled because of unresolved issues relating to resulting general offer.

- US$700 million pan-Asian mobile satellite project, involving Singapore Telecom and Singapore Technologies, expected to break even sometime in year 2002, three years after starts commercial operations.
- Creative Technology shares jump 80 Singapore cents to 20-week high of of S$9.80 after company announces return to profitability.
